meta.purpose: Analyst-side crisis library for the Cobalt Bank simulation. Use to (1) classify incoming dashboard announcements, (2) set severity priors and sanity bounds, (3) generate world/news/social feed items. NEVER paste real-world outcomes or 'what customers did' into persona prompts: personas must decide on their own.

evidence_tags.KISMEN: secondary news source read, primary filing not read
evidence_tags.DOGRULANAMADI: general knowledge / not checked today; do not cite on stage

how_to_use_in_code: crisis_classifier: match announcement text against archetypes[].signals -> pick 1-2 archetype ids, log the reading in TEAM_DOC.

world_feed: for the matched archetype, sample from world_feed_templates (news headline, social post, rival move) and inject into personas' 'what you saw this week' section, filtered by persona exposure attributes.
severity: scale with severity_prior (low/base/high); keep low/base/high as a parameter for experiments.
sanity_check: after a run, compare weekly losses with sanity_bounds; if exceeded, inspect prompts before trusting results.

calibration_anchors.what: UK bank TSB core banking migration failure (April 2018).
facts: Customer base about 5.2M; up to ~1.9-2M locked out, problems for weeks, BAU only by Dec 2018.
About 80,000 customers closed accounts in 2018 (~1.5% of 5.2M) while 140,000 new customers joined.
Total cost about GBP 330M incl. compensation, emergency recruitment (2,100 extra staff) and fraud losses.
Phishing/fake SMS wave impersonating the bank followed within weeks.
CEO stepped down; regulators fined about GBP 48.65M (Dec 2022).
calibration_anchors.use_for: Upper bound: a catastrophic, multi-week failure produced ~1.5% account closures and ~4% complaint rate over a year. A planned 36h read-only window should land far below this unless the announcement says otherwise.

calibration_anchors.what: Capital One multi-day outage via core/payment vendor FIS power failure (mid-January 2025, mid-month payday).
facts: Direct deposits and Early Pay credits delayed; most complaints were about deposits.
Customers criticised vague, slow updates; several threatened to close accounts once deposits arrived.
Full functionality restored for most customers by Saturday; class-action lawsuit followed.
calibration_anchors.use_for: Paycheck-timing outages hit paycheck-to-paycheck customers hardest; communication vagueness amplifies anger more than the outage itself. 'Threatened to close' is stated intent, not behaviour: good say-do gap example.

calibration_anchors.what: Silicon Valley Bank digital bank run (March 2023).
facts: USD 42B (~24% of deposits) withdrawn in one day; social media and private chat groups accelerated it.
Depositors were mostly uninsured (above USD 250k), concentrated, socially connected.
calibration_anchors.use_for: Tail-risk template for 'rumor' crises. Cobalt differs: retail, mostly insured, not one tight network. Only the 'savers with large balances' above the FDIC limit resemble SVB depositors. Use as an extreme bound, not a base case.

calibration_anchors.what: Fintech middleware Synapse bankruptcy (2024): 100k+ end users of apps like Yotta/Juno frozen for weeks/months, ledger shortfall.
facts: Frozen access for >100,000 customers; ~USD 160M still frozen by July 2024; shortfall estimates USD 65-96M.
Showed that 'FDIC-insured' messaging fails when the problem is a third party or the ledger.
calibration_anchors.use_for: Template for third-party/partner failure and for why FDIC reassurance alone may not calm customers who remember Synapse.

calibration_anchors.what: Phishing and fake-rebate SMS follow large outages (TSB 2018, Rogers Canada 2022 fake USD 90 rebate texts, CrowdStrike 2024 warnings).
calibration_anchors.use_for: If any outage or migration problem occurs, expect an impersonation wave within 1-2 weeks. A bank SMS sent during that window may be read as a scam.

calendar_context.context: Baseline week. Use it to check that nodecision reproduces BAU (about 1,800 complaints/month, 120 CFPB/month, rating 4.6).
Quiet. Rivals may start promotional rate campaigns ahead of holidays.
Thanksgiving and Black Friday: card volume peak; card-testing fraud and merchant breaches more likely; disputes rise in following weeks.
Cyber Monday; BAU migration email goes out Dec 5 (7 days before). First week customers learn the date if Cobalt says nothing earlier. Rivals know the date.
KNOWN CRISIS: Fri Dec 11 payday, Sat Dec 12 00:00 - Sun Dec 13 12:00 CT read-only, card offline cap USD 100/payment, may overrun 'some hours'. Holiday shopping weekend.
Aftermath: post-migration bugs, backlog, anger posts, reviews. Earliest week a decision can answer a week-6 surprise. A 4-week boost starting here ends exactly at Jan 10 measurement.
Christmas: spending peak, support staff holidays, gift-card and delivery scams.
New Year: credit card bills, resolutions to switch banks/save more; year-end rate comparisons.
Measurement week for all board goals. Any temporary boost that ended earlier no longer helps here.

archetypes.name: Migration runs longer than planned
archetypes.mechanism: Read-only extends into Sunday evening/Monday; bill payments, P2P and rent transfers blocked; offline USD 100 cap blocks larger purchases.
most_affected: paycheck customers living paycheck to paycheck
small business owners with card reader (weekend sales > USD 100)
world_feed_templates: News: 'Cobalt Bank customers still locked out of transfers hours after promised restart'
Social: 'Rent is due and my money is stuck in Cobalt read-only mode.'
Rival ad: 'Your bank down again? Switch in 5 minutes.'
menu_responses: Zero-interest advance up to USD 500 (paycheck group)
message_rules: Never promise an exact end time; say 'expected' and commit to update cadence.
Say what still works (cards up to the cap, balances visible).

archetypes.name: Wrong balances, duplicate or missing transactions after the switch
archetypes.mechanism: Trust shock: 'is my money safe?'. Large-balance savers check balances, some move money once transfers reopen. Complaints and CFPB filings spike.
world_feed_templates: Reddit: 'My Cobalt balance shows $0 after the update, anyone else?'
News: 'Regulator asks Cobalt about post-migration errors'
message_rules: State facts known, what is not known, and that deposits are FDIC-insured up to the limit (true statement).
Avoid 'everything is fine' before it is verified.

archetypes.name: Direct deposits arrive late (payroll processor / ACH / bank-side delay)
archetypes.mechanism: Hits the 310k paycheck customers; rent, bills and overdraft fears. Early pay and advances are the direct fix.
key_attributes: Cobalt is their main or second bank
world_feed_templates: Social: 'Payday and nothing in my Cobalt account.'
Coworker: 'Mine came in at the big bank this morning.'
menu_responses: Early pay (permanent, if not used yet)
message_rules: Do not claim Cobalt is not responsible unless confirmed; say when funds will post if known.

archetypes.name: Impersonation SMS/email/calls using the migration as a pretext
archetypes.mechanism: Scammers exploit the known date ('verify your account for the new system'). Victims lose money; everyone becomes suspicious of real bank messages, including paid SMS.
key_attributes: how they react to a text message from a bank
has been a victim of card fraud or phishing
world_feed_templates: Fake SMS text shown to persona: 'Cobalt: your account will be frozen during migration, verify here: cobalt-secure-verify.co'
News: 'Scammers target Cobalt customers ahead of system upgrade'
message_rules: State clearly what Cobalt will never ask (password, codes, links in SMS).
Prefer in-app/push over paid SMS in this window.

archetypes.name: Card fraud spike or merchant/processor data breach exposing Cobalt cards
archetypes.mechanism: Unauthorized charges; disputes take 10 business days for provisional credit; complaints are already mostly about disputes.
key_attributes: has been a victim of card fraud or phishing
world_feed_templates: News: 'Holiday retailer breach exposes millions of cards'
Persona event: 'You see a $87 charge you do not recognise.'
message_rules: Tell customers exactly how to get a new card and how fast credit arrives.

archetypes.name: Rivals raise savings rates or target Cobalt customers around the migration date
archetypes.mechanism: Widens the 0.5-point gap; rate-chasers among large-balance savers move money; deposit goal at risk. Only ~7,900 large savers moving most of their money breaks the deposit goal (our estimate).
key_attributes: moves money for a better rate
world_feed_templates: Ad: 'Banking offline this weekend? Earn 1% more with us.'
Newsletter: 'Best savings rates this week' table where Cobalt is near the bottom.
menu_responses: Savings rate boost (time it to end Jan 10 if possible)
Boost on new money only (cheaper, fairness risk)
message_rules: Rates only at menu levels; state the 4-week duration honestly.

archetypes.name: Social media rumor that Cobalt is in trouble / 'get your money out before the switch'
archetypes.mechanism: Fear-driven outflows mainly from customers above or unsure about the FDIC limit; spread through social exposure; mostly followers of opinion leaders.
most_affected: savers with large balances above USD 250k
world_feed_templates: TikTok: 'Pull your money out of Cobalt before they switch systems.'
News fact-check: 'Is your money safe at Cobalt? What FDIC insurance covers.'
message_rules: FDIC facts must be exact (standard limit USD 250k per depositor, per bank, per ownership category).
Do not say 'no risk' or 'guaranteed' beyond the insured limit.

archetypes.name: Third-party outage (card processor, cloud, P2P network, payroll provider)
archetypes.mechanism: Service disruption not caused by Cobalt but felt as Cobalt's failure; especially painful if close to the migration ('they are not ready').
world_feed_templates: Downdetector spike screenshot
Social: 'First the migration, now this?'
menu_responses: Offline limit increase (if card-related and before migration)
message_rules: Own the customer impact even if a vendor caused it; avoid blame-shifting tone.

archetypes.name: Card reader / merchant settlement problems for the 42k small businesses
archetypes.mechanism: Lost sales on holiday weekends (offline cap), delayed payouts affect payroll and inventory; SMB owners are vocal on review sites.
most_affected: small business owners with a Cobalt card reader
world_feed_templates: Local news: 'Austin cafe owners say card payments failed during holiday market'
message_rules: Give SMBs concrete timing for payouts.

archetypes.name: Regulator inquiry or investigative article (dispute handling, fees, outage complaints)
archetypes.mechanism: Hits fairness and trust scores; increases CFPB filings ('others are complaining, so will I').
world_feed_templates: News: 'Customers say Cobalt disputes take weeks'
message_rules: No admission or denial beyond facts; describe concrete changes.

archetypes.name: Central bank rate move or rivals' rate changes after a policy meeting
archetypes.mechanism: Shifts the rate gap; rate-sensitive savers re-evaluate.
key_attributes: moves money for a better rate
world_feed_templates: News: 'Online banks adjust savings rates after Fed decision'

archetypes.name: Federal government shutdown or benefit delay hitting federal employees' paychecks
archetypes.mechanism: Federal-employee customers miss paychecks; need bridge liquidity. The catalog lists 'employer: federal government' which hints this may matter.
most_affected: paycheck customers employed by federal government
analogs: US 2018-19 shutdown spanned the holiday period (general knowledge)
world_feed_templates: News: 'Federal workers face missed paychecks over the holidays'
menu_responses: Zero-interest advance targeted to affected group
message_rules: Target only the affected group; make repayment terms explicit.

archetypes.name: Austin weather/power event or staff shortage cutting support capacity
archetypes.mechanism: Support waits rise from 4 min; unanswered customers escalate to CFPB and reviews.
world_feed_templates: Social: 'On hold with Cobalt for 70 minutes.'
message_rules: Tell customers which channel is fastest right now.

archetypes.name: App update bug, login/2FA failures, or dark-mode/UX regression after migration
archetypes.mechanism: Daily app checkers notice first; App Store rating drops quickly; mostly annoyance, little money movement.
world_feed_templates: App Store review: '1 star. New update logged me out and codes never arrive.'

sanity_bounds.note: Our priors, not facts. If a run exceeds these, check the simulation first (challenge rule).
sanity_bounds.reference: TSB catastrophic multi-week failure: ~1.5% closures, ~3.9% complainants over a year.
